attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The unresolved Yang-Mills estimate is a finite OS-matrix no-new-boundary-renormalization theorem for reflected Wilson products: after ordinary loop renormalization, prove that every mixed collar defect B is rank one, preferably B=1, or show that any residual defect is an already locked individual normalization.
steps: Start with regulated reflection positivity: for every cutoff (a,L), every collar distance \delta>0, and every finite family F_i in the positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, the matrix S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j) is positive semidefinite.
Use the cutoff-removal topology only at fixed \delta. If all reflected fixed-collar entries converge, the closed positive cone of finite Hermitian matrices gives N^{(\delta)}\ge0 in the continuum.
Let \delta\downarrow0. Entrywise convergence of N^{(\delta)} to N again preserves positivity, so the collar-limit matrix N is positive. Up to this point the proof is formal and valid.
The target OS matrix is not N but M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j). The missing bridge is therefore the trace comparison between N and M, not reflection positivity itself.

Assume a multiplicative boundary-defect expansion N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}. If B_{ij}=\overline{b_i}b_j with all b_i\neq0, then N=D^*MD. Since D is invertible, positivity of N implies positivity of M by congruence: y^*My=(D^{-1}y)^*N(D^{-1}y)\ge0.

Test necessity of this condition for a closed-cone-only proof. Normalize a two-observable Wilson defect to B_{11}=B_{22}=1 and B_{12}=\beta. If |\beta|<1, choose 1<r<|\beta|^{-1} and set M_{12}=r e^{-i\arg\beta}. Then M is indefinite, but B\circ M is positive. Thus collar positivity can hold while target positivity fails.

This exhibits the exact role of the same-theory condition: individual congruences are harmless, but pair-dependent damping or mixed boundary contact terms can manufacture a positive collar-limit matrix without proving OS positivity for the intended Yang-Mills Schwinger functions.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is complete as finite-dimensional linear algebra, but it does not prove the analytic trace comparison for continuum Yang-Mills Wilson observables. The hard missing input is control of cusp, hairpin, perimeter, and reflection-plane contact terms as \Theta T_\delta W_i and T_\delta W_j collide at t=0, plus OS-density of the selected gauge-invariant core.

assumptions: For every cutoff pair (a,L) and every finite family in the positive-time gauge-invariant algebra, the regulated OS matrix is positive semidefinite.
For each fixed collar distance \delta>0, the cutoff-removal topology gives convergence of every reflected matrix entry S_{a,L}(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j).
The limit \delta\downarrow0 of fixed-collar continuum matrices exists as N_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j).
The intended target matrix is M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j), and the trace comparison is multiplicative on the chosen finite family: N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}.
The rank-one factors b_i, when present, are nonzero and do not change the observable algebra; they are only individual normalizations, not mixed boundary data.
definitions: source object: cutoff Yang-Mills gauge-invariant Schwinger functionals S_{a,L} on a locked positive-time algebra A_+ with collar embeddings T_\delta and regulated reflection-positive matrices Q_{a,L}(T_\delta F,c).
target object: continuum OS-positive Schwinger functional S on the intended non-collared gauge-invariant algebra A_+ producing the physical OS Hilbert pre-inner product.

controlled interface: for each finite family F_1,\ldots,F_n, the RG limit controls fixed-collar reflected matrix entries and the collar trace has an entrywise defect representation N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}.

same-theory condition: the defect B must be identically one or a nonzero rank-one congruence B_{ij}=\overline{b_i}b_j coming from observable normalizations already included in the locked theory, with no pair-dependent boundary counterterm.

equations.label: fixed-collar OS matrix
equations.valid_when: The collar keeps all reflected supports away from the reflection plane and the RG limit is valid for those reflected probes.

equations.label: boundary-defect comparison
equations.valid_when: The collar trace exists entrywise and no additive contact term remains after the locked renormalizations.

equations.label: rank-one congruence transfer
equations.valid_when: The defect is purely individual and the same-theory condition permits the diagonal normalization.

equations.label: two-by-two nonfactorizing falsifier
equations.valid_when: Then M has eigenvalue 1-r<0 while B\circ M is positive; this is valid as a logical obstruction to any proof using only positivity of the collar matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Compute the normalized mixed Wilson defect \beta_{CD}=B_{CD}/(B_{CC}B_{DD})^{1/2}. If |\beta_{CD}|<1 after all locked individual loop renormalizations, that is a falsifier for the same-theory closed-cone bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma isolates the exact finite-dimensional bridge from collar OS positivity to target OS positivity and explains why mixed Wilson-loop boundary anomalies are dangerous: only zero or rank-one defects are harmless for the closed-cone argument.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite OS-matrix boundary-defect transfer lemma: fixed-collar reflection positivity transfers to the intended non-collared continuum OS matrix if the collar trace defect is zero or a nonzero rank-one congruence already belonging to the locked observable normalization. More sharply, if the normalized Wilson boundary defect is a non-rank-one positive correlation matrix, then closed-cone positivity of the collar limit is not by itself a valid proof of positivity for the target Schwinger functions; a two-dimensional falsifier matrix can make the collar matrix positive while the intended matrix is indefinite.

assumptions: The reflected Wilson products have finite continuum expectations after the ordinary perimeter, corner, and composite renormalizations already locked into the observable definitions.
The ratios B_{ij} exist for the selected finite family or have a controlled asymptotic expansion whose leading term can be compared.
The target entries used in the ratios are not zero; if some are zero, the detector must be applied to additive defects or to a nearby nonzero subfamily.
definitions: Let W_i be mirror-smooth positive-time Wilson observables and T_\delta W_i their collars.
Define the mixed defect ratio, when the denominator is nonzero, by B_{ij}=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}S(\Theta T_\delta W_i,T_\delta W_j)/S(\Theta W_i,W_j).
A rank-one same-theory defect has the form B_{ij}=\overline{b_i}b_j with nonzero b_i.

equations.label: rank-one minor vanishing
equations.valid_when: The boundary defect is an individual congruence rather than pair-dependent mixed data.

equations.label: normalized two-loop defect
equations.valid_when: B_{ii},B_{jj}>0. A positive value of \mu_{ij} is a two-loop falsifier for rank-one factorization.

equations.label: Wilson ratio to test
equations.valid_when: The continuum functional S is already defined on both collared and target Wilson observables in the same gauge-invariant algebra.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A single nonzero \Delta_{ik;j\ell}, or a two-loop value \mu_{ij}>0 after individual renormalizations are removed, is a falsifier of the same-theory interface even if a boundary-renormalized positive theory still exists.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This supplies a concrete diagnostic for the missing Yang-Mills estimate: instead of asking abstractly whether OS positivity survives, one computes whether the mixed collar trace defect has rank one.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Multiplicative-minor detector for Wilson boundary defects: for a finite family of Wilson observables with nonzero target OS entries, a same-theory collar trace defect is rank one only if all 2-by-2 multiplicative minors vanish. Any nonzero minor is evidence of a pair-dependent cusp, hairpin, or boundary-contact anomaly that cannot be absorbed by individual Wilson-loop normalizations.

assumptions: The continuum Schwinger distributions for these local composites are tempered distributions away from coincident-point singularities already handled by the standard composite renormalization.
The smearing family T_\delta f converges to f in the test-function topology used to define the local Schwinger distributions.
Mirror-flatness prevents an extra reflection-plane boundary distribution from being sampled in the limit.
definitions: Let O_\alpha(x) be renormalized local gauge-invariant composites and F_i=\sum_\alpha O_\alpha(f_{i,\alpha}) with f_{i,\alpha} smooth, positive-time supported, and mirror-flat at t=0.
Let T_\delta act by translating or smoothing the supports into t\ge\delta without changing the locked composite-field normalization.
The target matrix is M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j).
The collar matrix is N^{(\delta)}_{ij}=S(\Theta T_\delta F_i,T_\delta F_j).

equations.label: distributional collar continuity
equations.valid_when: The reflected product is a renormalized distribution acting continuously on the chosen mirror-flat test functions.

equations.label: local-core defect
equations.latex: B_{ij}=1\quad\text{for all local mirror-flat core entries}
equations.valid_when: No new boundary counterterm appears at t=0 for the chosen local core.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonzero reflection-plane contact distribution acting on mirror-flat local smearing would be a severe falsifier, because it would show boundary renormalization is needed even before entering the Wilson sector.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This separates a plausibly valid local-density route from the Wilson-loop obstruction and provides a base case for OS-density arguments.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Mirror-flat local core trace lemma: for local gauge-invariant composite fields smeared by test functions supported in positive time and flat to sufficiently high order at the reflection plane, the collar trace defect should be B=1, so the fixed-collar closed-cone argument extends to the plane by ordinary distributional continuity. This lemma is a sanity check showing that the real obstruction is nonlocal Wilson geometry rather than every boundary approach.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot away from this branch if a standard Wilson-loop renormalization theorem shows unavoidable nonfactorizing mixed boundary defects at t=0, because then the pure RG closed-cone route proves positivity only for a boundary-modified theory.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote the bridge if one proves that all finite reflected Wilson collar defects have vanishing multiplicative minors after locked renormalization, and that the mirror-flat local/Wilson core is OS-dense in the intended gauge-invariant test algebra.
control_decision.reason: The branch made real progress by replacing the vague same-theory obstruction with a rank-one congruence criterion and an explicit two-dimensional falsifier. The next work should not revisit the closed-cone topology; it should compute or bound the Wilson boundary-defect matrix.

falsifiers: A two-loop Wilson pair with normalized mixed defect |B_{12}|/(B_{11}B_{22})^{1/2}<1 after locked individual renormalizations; this is a direct falsifier because the explicit 2-by-2 matrix construction shows positivity need not transfer.
A nonzero multiplicative minor B_{ij}B_{k\ell}-B_{i\ell}B_{kj}; this detects a pair-dependent boundary anomaly incompatible with rank-one same-theory congruence.
An additive reflection-plane contact term C_{ij} in N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}+C_{ij} that cannot be represented by an existing local observable in the locked algebra.
A cusp or hairpin anomalous factor in mixed reflected Wilson products that depends on the relative geometry of W_i and W_j rather than on the individual loops.

The cutoff-removal topology controls separated Wilson loops but not the limit in which reflected supports approach the plane, so fixed-collar positivity remains valid but the trace bridge is unavailable.
The continuum construction changes the Wilson-loop algebra by adding boundary-renormalized observables; positivity may survive there, but that would be the wrong same-theory target.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 182 turns the previous nonfactorizing-anomaly warning into a precise finite-dimensional bridge theorem. The closed-cone argument gives positivity of the collar-limit matrix N, but the intended OS matrix M is protected only when the boundary trace defect is an invertible rank-one congruence. A normalized mixed Wilson damping |\beta|<1 is not a cosmetic anomaly: it gives an explicit 2-by-2 falsifier where N is positive and M is indefinite. Thus the remaining Yang-Mills problem is sharply localized: prove a finite OS-matrix no-new-boundary-renormalization theorem for reflected Wilson products, while the local mirror-flat sector remains plausibly valid by distributional continuity.

This gives the fastest concrete falsifier or evidence for the rank-one defect theorem.
